subject: gargoyle
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: cathedral gargoyle crouched on a ledge.
Style: gothic stone carving.

spec.name: Cathedral Gargoyle of the Rain-Ledge
spec.description: A gothic stone-carved gargoyle crouched on a mossy cathedral ledge, snarling over the edge with glowing amber eyes, folded wings rising behind it like a spire.
spec.layout: The model is a hunched gargoyle perched on a projecting cathedral cornice (the ledge), facing +Z and centred on x = 0. The ledge is the only floor piece: a weathered limestone slab 0.35 m tall, 2.8 wide and 2.8 deep, with a moulded drip edge at its front (z = +1.4), a copper rain-gutter channel along its top front, moss and lichen creeping from the cracks, and a grotesque carved waterspout face under the front lip. On it, the gargoyle crouches low and forward: heavy digitigrade haunches raised at the back (z around -0.3), a barrel chest leaning down over the front, knuckles and clawed hands gripping the ledge's front lip at z = +1.26 as if about to pounce, and a thick tail coiling out behind around the ledge base. The head juts forward over the edge at y = 1.6: a broad brow, swept-back curled stone horns, an open snarling jaw showing fangs, and two glowing amber eyes set deep under the brow. The signature feature is the wing pair: membrane wings half-folded, rising up and back behind the shoulders in a tall gothic arch to y = 2.5, their bony fingers and clawed tips reading like buttresses against the sky. Style on every part: faceted chisel-cut stone, flat colours by place (warm light-grey on top-facing surfaces, cool dark grey on undersides and shadow sides), rain-streak staining down vertical faces, moss on upward faces and in seams, verdigris copper on the gutter and waterspout, and fine detail carried by separate seated parts — carved seam lines, rivet-like pockmarks, brow ridges, cheek fluting, talon rings. Nothing floats: feet and tail rest on the ledge top, hands rest on the ledge lip, and every part's box abuts its neighbour's.

parts.builds: The cathedral cornice the gargoyle perches on: a chisel-cut limestone slab with a moulded profile (a step in, a roll, a drip edge) built from stacked frustumBoxes and slabs, front face at z = +1.4 with a protruding rounded lip at its top edge. Details as separate seated parts: a semicircular copper waterspout gargoyle face under the front lip centre (a crude open-mouthed carved face with ringed eyes, wearing copperVerdigris with copperDark hollows), the rain-gutter channel sunk along the ledge top front running left-right with copperVerdigris inner walls and lichen tufts in the corners, carved masonry joints (thin mortar-coloured recessed lines dividing the slab into ashlar blocks, mossDark tufts seated in two or three joints), pockmark chips on the top surface in stoneDeep, rain-streak staining in rainStain running down the front face from the lip, moss patches on the top and on the spout's shoulders, and small lichen discs scattered on the top corners. The bottom edge sits exactly on y = 0; a shallow corbel bracket slopes back under the slab at both ends so the ledge reads as projecting from an unseen wall behind z = -1.4. Uses the glow kit on nothing here — the ledge is lit stone only.
parts.attaches: Stands alone on y = 0; the other parts rest on ledgeTop (feet and tail at y = 0.35) and ledgeLip (hands gripping the front lip at [±0.42, 0.36, 1.26]). Keep the top surface at exactly y = 0.35 from z = -1.2 to +1.1 and the lip front at z = 1.26 to 1.32 so the limb builder's contact points land cleanly.

parts.builds: The gargoyle's crouched body from hips to neck, built skeleton-first on the hips, chest and tail joints: a loft or swept spine curve from the raised haunches (behind and above the hips joint, rump peak at [0, 1.15, -0.6]) down a hunched back to the deep chest (widest at chest, belly hanging to y = 0.42 at z = +0.2), with the neck emerging from the chest top toward neckSocket. Chest stone is stoneLight on the upper back catching light, stone on the sides, stoneDark under the belly, with rainStain streaks painted down the flanks and moss tufts seated along the spine ridge and in the shoulder-blade hollows. Carved details as seated parts: two rows of chiselled abdominal blocks on the belly (small stoneDeep slabs), a spine ridge of triangular carved vertebra studs from rump to neck, deep furrowed shoulder plates (fluted stone slabs) framing the shoulder and wing sockets, and a scored sternum plate. Includes the ribcage suggestion: three faint rib ridges per side as thin curved stoneDark rods on the flanks. The tail is a tapering swept tube on the tail joint with 4 tail sub-joints the builder adds under 'tail' (tail2..tail4, roles tail): it flows out behind and to the right, curling around at the ledge level and resting its tufted tip (a barbed arrow-cluster of stoneDeep spikes) on ledgeTop near [0.7, 0.35, -0.9], with carved segment rings every few centimetres as thin stoneDeep bands.
parts.attaches: Owns the hips, chest and tail joints. Its chest front slope meets the neck at neckSocket for the head part; the shoulder plates frame shoulderL/R where the limb part's arms hang; the rump flanks meet hipSocketL/R for the legs; the back meets wingRootL/R where the wing part's wing arms root. Nothing crosses x = 0 except the spine and tail base.

parts.builds: The head and the face, the model's focal point, built on the head and jaw joints and sized from one head region scale constant so every feature stays locked to the skull. Skull: a faceted wedge-skull sweeping from the brow down a short heavy muzzle toward +Z, brow ridge overhanging the eyes in a heavy stoneLight slab, cheeks fluted with chisel-cut stoneDark grooves, and the crown scoring with chisel marks. The signature horns: two thick swept-back horns rooting at the crown's outer corners, curling up and back in a gothic crook (spiral paths, hornStone, tips in hornTip, each with 3 raised segment rings and a chiselled spiral groove). A third small median horn spike on the forehead above the brow. Ears: two small pointed stoneDark bat-ear flanges behind the horns. The face: two deep eye sockets cut under the brow, each holding a glowing eye — a faceted amber orb with an ember-red slit pupil part seated in front, glow kit on both at strength 1.4 so they burn out of the shadow. A broad flat nose with two nostril recesses, cheek jowls, and furrowed brow chevrons. The jaw is a separate lower jaw on the jaw joint, dropped open in a snarl: upper and lower fang rows (4 fangs per side in teeth, canines long, seated in gum-coloured sockets), a tongue of tongue-coloured stone lolling forward, and a chin tuft. Behind the head, the neck the torso builder left at neckSocket is capped by a thick mane-like carved collar of overlapping stone scales the head part owns.
parts.attaches: Rides head and jaw, which parent from neck at neckSocket. The jaw hinge sits at [0, 1.5, 0.5]; the closed geometry must clear the torso's chest top. Horns stay inside x = ±0.42 and above y = 1.9 to keep out of the wings' box.

parts.builds: Arms, legs and their claws, built on the arm and leg joints with IK so every contact lands exactly. Legs: digitigrade crouch through limb() from each hip socket — thigh mass back and up, knee forward, hock back, toes forward — planted with soles flat on ledgeTop at [±0.42, 0.35, -0.1] (front foot) and the trailing hind foot perched on the ledge's back edge at [±0.5, 0.35, -1.1] with the heel overhanging, for the perched tension. Each limb is a swept tube thickening at thigh and calf (stone, stoneDark on the underside, stoneLight on the shin tops), with carved knee plates (fluted stoneLight studs), hock spurs, and 3 forward toes plus a rear dewclaw per foot: segmented toes in stone ending in long curved talons in claw with a lighter wear ring at each base, gripping the ledge top so the talon tips visibly curl over the lip. Arms: from each shoulder socket the arm hangs down and forward to the ledge lip, elbow back and out, forearm landing with the knuckles on ledgeLip at [±0.42, 0.36, 1.26]: a heavy fist with 3 thick fingers curled over the lip edge plus an opposing thumb, each finger a 2-segment rod with a claw talon hooked down the ledge's front face. Details: elbow and knuckle stone studs, forearm bracer-like carved bands, moss tufts in the elbow creases, and a fine rainStain streak down each forearm where water would run off the fist.
parts.attaches: Legs ride legL/legR rooted at hipSocketL/R (torso's rump wraps them); arms ride armL/armR rooted at shoulderL/R (torso's shoulder plates frame them). Feet contact ledgeTop, fists contact ledgeLip — both mounts on the ledge part. Fingers reaching below y = 0.35 only on the ledge's front face, never below y = 0.

parts.builds: The folded wing pair, the silhouette's signature: half-cloaked wings rising up and back behind the shoulders in a tall pointed gothic arch, like carved buttresses framing the head. Each wing is built on its wing joint with 4 wing sub-joints the builder adds (wingL2..4 / wingR2..4, role wing) sweeping out, up and back — the leading-edge arm a tapering bone tube in stone with stoneDark joints, carrying 4 long bony fingers fanning to the arch tips (highest finger tip at y = 2.45 near x = ±0.95, others descending back to z = -0.95). Between the fingers, membrane skins (b.membrane) in membraneWarm with stoneDark outer panels and rainStain streaks painted along the finger lines, scalloped between each finger so the trailing edge reads as carved drapery. Chisel detail: a raised rib rod along each finger, a row of small stone studs along the wing's leading edge, and two large carved rosette bosses (lichen-coloured discs with carved petals) seated where the membrane meets the humerus. Each wing tip ends in a hooked claw talon in claw. The wings' inner root blends into a thick shoulder scapula shield per side that overlaps the torso's shoulder plates without touching the arms. Small moss tufts root in the membrane's lowest folds near the back. The arch leaves a clear window between the horns (up to y = 2.15, |x| < 0.42) and the wing fingers.
parts.attaches: Rides wingL and wingR rooted at wingRootL/R on the chest; the wing roots overlap the torso's shoulder plates by burying their first radius into the rump/back mass. Fingers and membrane stay behind z = 0.35 so nothing covers the face, and above the torso's back line except at the buried roots.

calls.reasoning:
I'm writing a spec JSON for a cathedral gargoyle crouched on a ledge, gothic stone carving style. Need to split into 3-6 parts, mounts, joints (static model can have empty joints, but a creature... it's a monster; could be rigged, but posing complexity — crouched gargoyle. Since multiple builders build independently, a skeleton spec helps consistency. Let me define joints: spine, hips, chest, neck, head, jaw, arms, legs, wings. But each part lists joints its geometry rides. Keep manageable.

Model: gargoyle crouched on a stone ledge. The ledge is scenery named in the pitch, so include it as a part. Size: gargoyle crouched maybe 1.6m tall, wingspan ~2.6m. Ledge maybe 2.2 wide × 2.6 deep. Facing +Z (gargoyle faces out over the ledge front).

Parts:
1. ledge — stone ledge/cornice with gutter, moss, weathering. box roughly x -1.3..1.3, y 0..0.35, z -1.3..1.3. floor: true.
2. body — crouched torso, hips, haunches, spine, chest, ribs, belly. box y 0.3..1.4 roughly, z -0.8..0.5.
3. head — head with horns, brow, snout, jaw joint, fangs, ears. attaches at neck mount.
4. limbs — arms, hands with claws gripping ledge front, legs digitigrade, feet claws. Could split: forelimbs and hindlimbs, or one "limbs" part. 3-6 parts, even richness. Maybe: ledge, body, head, wings, limbs (front+back). 5 parts.
5. wings — folded/cloaking wings rising behind, membranes, ribs, claws on wing tips. Wings half-spread/cloaked upward, adds height. Size height maybe 2.4.

Joints: since builders never see each other's code, joints must be specified in the spec with positions. Define skeleton:

- root "hips" at [0, 0.75, -0.1]? Crouched gargoyle: haunches raised, hunched over, hands on ledge front edge. Let's set proportions.

Let me lay out coordinates. Ledge top at y = 0.35. Gargoyle crouches on ledge: feet on ledge top, hands gripping front edge of ledge (at z = 1.3 front). Hips at [0, 0.95, -0.35], chest at [0, 1.25, 0.05], neck [0, 1.5, 0.25], head [0, 1.65, 0.4]. Head top with horns up to ~2.2. Wings rise to 2.4.

Joint list (parents first):
- body (spine root) at [0, 0.95, -0.3], dir [0, 0.35, 1] (leaning forward)
- chest at [0, 1.25, 0.05], parent body, role spine
- neck at [0, 1.45, 0.25], parent chest, dir [0, 0.4, 1]
- head at [0, 1.6, 0.42], parent neck, dir [0, 0.25, 1], role head
- jaw at head, role jaw
- wingL parent chest at [0.28, 1.35, -0.25], dir [1, 0.8, -0.6], role wing
- wingR mirrored
- armL parent chest at [0.3, 1.2, 0.15], dir [0.6, -0.8, 0.4], role arm
- armR
- legL parent body at [0.3, 0.85, -0.35], dir [0.4, -1, 0.2], role leg
- legR
- handL digit at ledge front? Keep to main joints; parts can add sub-joints (fingers, wing fingers, jaw). The spec says joints created in order before parts; each part lists joints its geometry rides. Sub-joints could be created by the part builders themselves (they can create joints). But spec says "joints is the skeleton, created in this order before any part runs". So sub-joints like fingers can be added by builder within their part? The contract: "joints: created in this order before any part runs". Probably part builders may create extra joints under their listed ones. To be safe, include key ones in spec and allow parts to add small sub-joints (digits, wing phalanges) as children, noted in the part description.

Mounts: ledgeTop [0, 0.35, 0], ledgeFrontLip [0, 0.35, 1.28], neckSocket [0, 1.45, 0.25]... mounts are shared points where parts meet: 
- ledgeTop: [0, 0.35, -0.1] — where feet sit
- ledgeLip: [0, 0.36, 1.25] — where hands grip the front edge
- shoulderLine for wings/arms attach to chest — that's within body part? Actually chest is part of "body" part; wings and arms attach at sockets on the chest. Mounts: wingSocketL [0.3, 1.32, -0.2], armSockets, hipSockets, neckSocket.

Simplify parts: 
1. ledge (floor)
2. torso (body incl. chest, spine, hips, haunches, tail maybe) — gargoyles sometimes have tails. Add a tail curling. Yes, tail adds character. Tail part of torso or limbs? Give tail to torso.
3. head (with horns, jaw)
4. limbs (arms + legs + claws)
5. wings

Budgets sum ≤ 900; total parts maybe ~300-400. Budget: ledge 60, torso 120, head 100, limbs 120, wings 90. Sum 490. Fine.

Palette (≤24): weathered limestone greys, darker basalt shadow, moss green, verdigris, amber eye glow (glow kit!), tongue, teeth bone, horn darker stone, copper gutter, mortar.

Colors:
- stoneLight "#9a968c" (sunlit limestone)
- stone "#7d7a72" main
- stoneDark "#5a5854" shadow sides/underside
- stoneDeep "#46443f"
- moss "#5e7a3c"
- mossDark "#3f5626"
- lichen "#b8a878"
- horn "#4a463e" (darker polished horn-stone)
- hornTip "#35322c"
- teeth "#c9c2ae"
- eyeGlow "#ffb23e" amber glowing eyes
- eyeEmber "#ff7a1e"
- tongue "#7a3a48"
- gum "#5a2c34"
- copper "#7a9a8a" verdigris copper gutter
- copperDark "#4e6a5e"

- wingMembrane stone-dark "#55524c" — membrane as stone, maybe with warmer inner "#6e6455"
- claw "#3c3a34"

That's ~20. Good.

Mounts:
- ledgeTop [0, 0.35, -0.05]
- ledgeLip [0, 0.36, 1.26]
- neckSocket [0, 1.48, 0.28]
- shoulderL [0.32, 1.3, -0.05], shoulderR [-0.32, 1.3, -0.05]
- hipL [0.3, 0.9, -0.3], hipR
- wingRootL [0.3, 1.38, -0.3], wingRootR
- tailRoot [0, 0.75, -0.75]

Size: width 2.8 (wings spread partly; folded rising wings span maybe 2.6), height 2.5 (horns + wings), depth 2.8 (tail back + hands front). Say [2.8, 2.5, 2.8].

Layout text: describe silhouette from front: crouched hunched gargoyle perched on a projecting stone ledge/cornice; forward-facing, hands gripping the front lip, digitigrade feet planted on the ledge top, folded wings rising like a gothic spire behind the shoulders, horned head jutting forward over the ledge edge, snarling open jaw, glowing amber eyes, tail curled around the base.

Joints list — keep simple, static model? It's a monster; rigging could be nice but for a posed statue, static is fine and joints optional. But spec says role list from system prompt; providing joints makes it riggable and the spec sample includes them. I'll provide joints. But multiple builders: each part lists joints it rides. I'll specify joints: root "spine0" at hips... Let me name:

- "hips" [0, 0.9, -0.3], dir [0, 0.5, 1], role spine — root
- "chest" parent hips, [0, 1.2, 0.05], dir [0, 0.6, 1], role spine
- "neck" parent chest, [0, 1.42, 0.22], dir [0, 0.55, 1], role neck
- "head" parent neck, [0, 1.58, 0.38], dir [0, 0.3, 1], role head
- "jaw" parent head, [0, 1.5, 0.5], dir [0, 0.15, 1]... jaw role jaw
- "wingL" parent chest, [0.3, 1.34, -0.22], dir [0.75, 0.65, -0.55], role wing
- "wingR" parent chest, mirrored dir [-0.75, 0.65, -0.55]
- "armL" parent chest, [0.34, 1.22, 0.1], dir [0.5, -0.75, 0.55], role arm
- "armR" mirrored
- "legL" parent hips, [0.3, 0.85, -0.3], dir [0.35, -1, 0.1], role leg
- "legR" mirrored
- "tail" parent hips, [0, 0.72, -0.6], dir [0, -0.2, -1], role tail

Parts' joints lists:
- ledge: [] (static, plain objects)
- torso: hips, chest, tail
- head: head, jaw (plus neck? head part builds head; neck could be torso). Neck geometry to torso part.
- limbs: armL, armR, legL, legR (plus digits they add)
- wings: wingL, wingR

Each part box:
- ledge: x[-1.4,1.4], y[0,0.38], z[-1.4,1.4]
- torso: x[-0.55,0.55], y[0.3,1.5], z[-0.85,0.45]
- head: x[-0.4,0.4], y[1.35,2.1], z[0.1,0.85]
- limbs: x[-0.75,0.75], y[0.35,1.45], z[-0.7,1.3] (feet on ledge top y 0.35+, hands on lip)
- wings: x[-1.4,1.4], y[1.2,2.5], z[-1.0,0.3]

Write description, layout, then parts with builds text, attaches, budget.
